text:
Priya: spotted something odd in partner-ci-artifacts s3: object key ci/builds/2026-03-22/nested_blob.bin begins with `vault:v1:` but then contains `aws-kms:` marker after the transit header. Looks like a nested envelope (KMS-encrypted payload that was later transit-wrapped).
sec-bot: Alert: external-object-read detected on partner-ci-artifacts (rule: s3-external-access). Created incident 3581239999.
Noah: paste exact s3 uri + first ~120 chars (no plaintext) so we can fingerprint the wrapper.
Priya: s3://partner-ci-artifacts/ci/builds/2026-03-22/nested_blob.bin
Priya: header (sanitized): `vault:v1:ab12cd... || aws-kms:arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01` -> definitely a KMS envelope inside transit wrapper.
Keiko: that increases blast radius. If partner had read-only access to the file, they could upload it elsewhere, and if someone had KMS Decrypt on that KMS key (or a grant) and also had transit/unwrap, mixing of key boundaries could be abused.
Irfan: plan-of-action (containment): 1) revoke partner read binding 2) disable any partner SA/keys 3) quarantine the object (copy to a secure bucket with restricted ACLs and delete original) 4) enable/inspect Vault & KMS audit logs for unwrap/decrypt events 5) rotate both Vault transit key and the referenced KMS key if there is any indication of access.
Oncall: executing containment now. Commands run: 
  # revoke GCP binding (if GCP SA)
  gcloud projects remove-iam-policy-binding infra-onboard --member="serviceAccount:partner-ci@partner-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com" --role="roles/storage.objectViewer"
  # quarantine: copy -> set lock -> delete
  aws s3 cp s3://partner-ci-artifacts/ci/builds/2026-03-22/nested_blob.bin s3://sec-quarantine/3581239999/nested_blob.bin --profile=infra-admin
  aws s3api put-object-acl --bucket sec-quarantine --key 3581239999/nested_blob.bin --acl private
  aws s3 rm s3://partner-ci-artifacts/ci/builds/2026-03-22/nested_blob.bin --profile=infra-admin
  # disable partner keys (example)
  gcloud iam service-accounts keys list --iam-account=partner-ci@partner-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com
  gcloud iam service-accounts keys delete KEY_ID --iam-account=partner-ci@partner-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com
Priya: I've also started a scan for other objects that contain both `vault:` and `aws-kms:` markers in all partner buckets. Found 3 matches so far. List uploaded to /sec/artifacts/3581239999-objects.txt (scrubbed).
Jason: forensics: check Vault audit for transit/rewrap/unwrap and AWS CloudTrail for KMS Decrypt/GenerateDataKey operations referencing that key ARN. Example queries: 
  # Vault transit unwrap lines
  cat /var/log/vault_audit.log | jq -c 'select(.path|contains("transit/unwrap") )' | grep partner-ci
  # CloudTrail example
  aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=ResourceName,AttributeValue=arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01 --max-results 50
Irfan: if CloudTrail shows grants or decrypts from unexpected principals, rotate the KMS key (create new key, re-encrypt data keys, and retire old key). Note: AWS KMS key rotation cannot rewrap external ciphertexts, so we need to generate new DataKey and re-encrypt payloads where we have plaintext or rewrap via Vault if possible.
Keiko: sample steps we might take: 1) create new KMS CMK, 2) request partner to provide re-encryption plan if they control the inner ciphertext, OR 3) if we have original plaintext in-store, re-encrypt with new CMK and transit rewrap. If none of those, we treat inner KMS envelope as potentially exposed and mark artifacts as invalid.
Maria: enable audit sinks and retain 180 days for both Vault transit audit and AWS CloudTrail slice for the key ARN. Push logs to central-logging and to the incident ticket.
Legal: looped in; partner/SOC notified with scrubbed list. Legal asked for timestamps, containment commands, and evidence of deletion/quarantine. Priya: please capture copy commands and checksums.
Priya: done, checksums for quarantined objects uploaded: sha256:3f8a... (stored in /sec/artifacts/3581239999-checksums.txt).
Oncall: locking down policies: remove any primitive `vault:transit/*` grants from broad roles, add explicit allow for `transit/encrypt/*` for build-service, and explicit allow for `transit/rewrap` only for migration jobs. Update IAM condition to limit partner role to specific object prefixes only.
Irfan: example Vault policy HCL (tighten decrypt):
  path "transit/encrypt/*" { capabilities = ["update"] }
  path "transit/decrypt/*" { capabilities = ["deny"] }
  # create a specific internal path for rewrap/migration with narrow principals
  path "transit/rewrap" { capabilities = ["update"] }

Jason: timeline so far: 2026-03-22T02:10Z object discovery -> 02:15Z revocation + quarantine -> 02:30Z partner/SOC notif -> 03:05Z CloudTrail/Vault audit checks started.
Keiko: next steps and owners:
  - Priya: finish full scan across partner buckets + upload scrubbed list (ETA 2h)
  - Noah: lead KMS forensics + determine if key was used (ETA 3h)
  - Irfan: prepare transit key rotation + rewrap playbook (coord with runtime) (ETA 4h)
  - Jason: compile audit timeline and evidence for Legal (ETA 3h)
  - Oncall: keep quarantine locked and verify deletion from partner buckets (ongoing)
Priya: will also run a quick grep on CI logs to ensure no codepath is writing nested envelopes (looking for patterns: `generate-data-key` followed by `vault write transit/encrypt`).
Noah: if we find automated pipelines doing nested wrap, we'll patch them to either rely on a single envelope mechanism or use envelope encryption with clear ownership boundaries.
Maria: schedule a 60-minute post-incident review tomorrow 16:00 UTC to validate rewraps, KMS rotations, and RBAC changes. Also draft a short customer/partner note for transparency.
Legal: thanks, we'll prepare a notification template and loop in Privacy if needed.
Jason: nice work catching the nested-wrapper pattern early. Keep updates here; please paste CloudTrail/Vault audit snippets (sanitized) into the ticket. :lock:
